title: Web: load-older trigger + scroll preservation + poll sequencing
action: Add a 'load older' trigger to the terminal-detail screen (web/src/views/terminal.ts) fired when the operator scrolls/swipes .term-viewport to its top: call the new ?history=1 endpoint (web/src/api.ts) and do a full wholesale re-render with the result via the existing applyScreen() path (term.reset()+write — NOT a prepend; applyScreen has no prepend path, per plan.md's Discovery). Raise or otherwise account for the 400-row render clamp (terminal.ts:168, `rows = clamp(lines.length+1, 4, 400)`) so 'load older' can actually surface more than 400 rows of returned history — otherwise the clamp silently discards it before the operator ever sees it. Add explicit scroll-position handling for the two cases plan.md's risk map identifies: (a) when total content crosses the 400-row clamp or herdr's 1000-line cap, the oldest visible rows age out of the window and scrollTop must be adjusted rather than left stale; (b) a content shrink, where term.resize() running before term.reset() (:169-170) can otherwise clamp scrollTop irrecoverably. Add an in-flight guard so the existing 1500ms poll loop (setInterval at :309, poll() at :174-187 with zero existing overlap protection) can never interleave with an in-flight history-load request's read-then-restore-to-bottom round trip — build this from scratch, there is no existing guard to reuse. Add a real DOM-level test exercising renderTerminal's actual behavior for the load-older trigger, the 400-row/scroll-position handling, and the poll/history sequencing — the pre-existing web/test/terminal.test.ts only covers computeKeyboardInset/stripAnsiLen/terminalHead helpers, which is not coverage of this cell's behavior.

truths: Scrolling .term-viewport to its top while viewing a pane's history triggers exactly one history request, not a request per scroll event
History returned via ?history=1 that exceeds 400 rows is actually rendered/reachable by the operator, not silently clamped away
The operator's reading position is preserved across a normal poll tick while scrolled up reading history, including across a 400-row/1000-line ceiling crossing and a content-shrink case
The existing 1500ms poll and a history-load request never interleave their reads/writes to the same pane
At least one test exercises renderTerminal's actual DOM behavior for these paths, not only helper functions
prohibitions: Do not remove or bypass the existing applySheetInset scroll-to-bottom behavior for the Type/Keys sheets
Do not implement a prepend path — applyScreen's wholesale-replace design is the actual mechanism, per plan.md

verify: cd web && npm run test -- --run terminal

trace.outcome: Web: 'load older' trigger on scroll-to-top calling ?history=1 via applyScreen's wholesale re-render; render row clamp raised 400->1000 (matches herdr's D2 cap); scroll-position preservation (distanceFromBottom-anchored, clamped) for ceiling-crossing and content-shrink cases; in-flight guard so the 1500ms poll and a history load never interleave; 6 new real DOM-level renderTerminal tests plus 4 preserveScrollTop unit tests added (20/20 passing, up from 10)
